science.title: Supercontinuum generation and absorption spectroscopy from 3 to 20 μm using a highly nonlinear telluride glass rod
science.description: Broadband light sources extending deep into the long-wavelength mid-infrared are of strong interest for molecular spectroscopy, sensing, and nonlinear photonics, but their generation remains challenging because of the limited availability of suitable materials and efficient nonlinear conversion schemes. Here, we demonstrate broadband supercontinuum generation in a bulk GeTe₄–AgI chalcohalide glass using intense femtosecond pulses centered at approximately 8.5 μm. The generated supercontinuum extends from 3 to 20 μm, corresponding to a spectral coverage of approximately 2.7 octaves, and reaches an output average power of 2.1 mW at a 1-kHz repetition rate. The high peak power relative to the estimated self-focusing critical power leads to strong nonlinear spectral broadening in the bulk glass, consistent with the regime of filamentation-assisted supercontinuum generation. The generated broadband source is further evaluated for long-wavelength mid-IR spectroscopy through absorption measurements of a 100-µm-thick polytetrafluoroethylene film. The main absorption features measured using the supercontinuum source agree well with those obtained using a conventional Fourier-transform infrared spectrometer, including characteristic bands around 16 and 18 μm. These results demonstrate the potential of telluride glasses for broadband nonlinear light generation and spectroscopy extending into the long-wavelength mid-IR.

science.title: Removal and biodegradation of the pharmaceutical pollutant cortisone acetate by Scenedesmus obtusus under varying salinity conditions
science.description: Pharmaceutical contaminants such as cortisone acetate pose a significant environmental challenge due to their persistence in aquatic systems and the limited effectiveness of conventional wastewater treatment processes. This study evaluated the potential of the microalga Scenedesmus obtusus for the removal and biodegradation of cortisone acetate under varying salinity, pH, and exposure time conditions. An artificial neural network model (ANN) was developed to predict system performance, and a genetic algorithm (GA) was subsequently applied to this model to identify optimal operational parameters, which confirming the influence of environmental factors on treatment efficiency. Under optimized conditions obtained by GA (zero salinity, pH 7, and a 10-day retention period), the model predicted a cortisone acetate removal efficiency of 96.18%, which closely matched the experimentally observed removal efficiency of 97.68%. Additionally, liquid chromatography–tandem mass spectrometry (LC–MS/MS) analysis identified several degradation byproducts, consistent with possible biotransformation of cortisone acetate rather than simple retention in algal biomass. Moreover, monitoring of chlorophyll a and b levels indicated increased photosynthetic activity and sustained biomass accumulation throughout the experiment, supporting effective pollutant removal. Scanning electron microscopy further revealed structural changes in the microalgal cells after treatment, including surface roughening and pore formation, consistent with cellular stress responses associated with pollutant exposure. These findings confirm the potential of Scenedesmus obtusus as a sustainable and efficient bioremediation agent for pharmaceutical pollutants in aquatic environments.

science.title: Development of an edible vaccine candidate conferring protective efficacy against pneumococcal challenge using conserved PspA epitopes in a murine model
science.description: Streptococcus pneumoniae, also known as pneumococcus, is one of the leading causes of respiratory tract infections, meningitis, and septicemia in Bangladesh. In recent years, the pneumococcal surface protein A (PspA) has been suggested as a promising candidate, alone or with other immunogens, to be included in a future vaccine. Edible plant-based vaccines use recombinant antigens produced in plant tissues, providing an affordable and oral delivery option compared to traditional vaccines. This study applied a computational reverse vaccinology strategy to identify four potential B-cell epitope peptides from the PspA. Four epitope peptide sequences were found as the most potential B cell epitopes. Conservancy analysis was done using in silico tools. The sequences of S. pneumoniae epitope sequences were analyzed and placed in fusion with alpha zein. Agrobacterium tumefaciens strain LBA4404 containing the Ti plasmid was used for selection in all cases for the integration of the gene of interest. Antigens of S. pneumoniae fused to zein in Lycopersicon esculentum were generated using Agrobacterium-mediated genetic transformation protocols. The transformation through A. tumefaciens was confirmed by kanamycin selection and PCR analysis with the specific primers. Mice immunized with transgenic plant tissue and the control mice were challenged intraperitoneally with 10 times the LD50 dose of the S. pneumoniae type 7F. The results demonstrated significant protection, with 83% of immunized mice surviving the live S. pneumoniae challenge compared to only 50% survival in control groups. These findings highlight the selected PspA epitope region as a promising target conferring protective efficacy in this murine model, supporting further development of an oral pneumococcal vaccine candidate.
